TYPICAL SPECIAL CONDITION (SC) AND INTENT FOR EACH SC \nFOR PARTS 23, 25, 27, AND 29\nSpecial Condition Requirement #1: \nSafe cell temperatures and pressures must be maintained during any foreseeable charging or \ndischarging condition and during any failure of the charging or battery monitoring system not \nshown to be extremely remote. The rechargeable lithium battery installation must preclude \nexplosion in the event of those failures. \nThe intent of this SC requirement: \nThe cells within the lithium battery system shall be designed to minimize the impact of \nself-sustained, uncontrolled increases in cell temperature or pressure, as a result of any \nforeseeable charging or discharging condition. The probability of this event must be shown to be \nextremely remote (1 event in 10 million (1x10-7) flight hours). It must preclude explosion in the \nevent of any failure.\nSpecial Condition Requirement #2: \nDesign of the rechargeable lithium batteries must preclude the occurrence of self-sustaining, \nuncontrolled increases in temperature or pressure. \nThe intent of this SC requirement: \nThe lithium battery system shall be designed to minimize the impact of self-sustained, \nuncontrolled increases in temperature or pressure, as a result of any failure within the battery. \nThe probability of impact must be extremely improbable (1 event in 1 billion (1x10-9) flight \nhours). \nSpecial Condition Requirement #3: \nNo explosive or toxic gases emitted by any rechargeable lithium battery in normal operation, \nor as the result of any failure of the battery charging system, monitoring system, or battery \ninstallation which is not shown to be extremely remote, may accumulate in hazardous quantities \nwithin the aircraft.\nThe intent of this SC requirement: \nThe battery system shall not emit any explosive or toxic gases, smoke, or fluids during normal \noperation except through designed venting provisions. \nBattery systems shall be capable of containing or safely relieving the maximum pressure buildup \nthat can occur under worst-case failure conditions. If the battery system is not capable of \ncontaining the maximum pressure, then the appropriate provisions shall be included to safely \nrelieve pressure from the battery. Emissions shall only escape through designed pressure \nrelief provisions. \nHazardous emissions may be flammable, explosive, corrosive, or toxic in certain concentrations. \nThe installer should work with the manufacturer to quantify and mitigate the effects of hazardous \nemissions. Clean as required.\n3.1.8.2 Inspect the battery for improper installation (loose terminal screws, battery \nterminal links, or connector).\n3.1.8.3 Inspect the battery mounting.\n3.1.8.4 Inspect for evidence of physical damage including heat \ndamage/discoloration.\n3.1.9 Batteries in a rotating stock must be functionally checked at the manufacturer’s \nrecommended inspection intervals. Some failure modes may include degraded charge \nretention capability, settling of particulates, or other damage due to prolonged storage.\nBatteries in rotating stock may also require periodic servicing per the manufacturer’s \ninstructions.\n3.2 Aircraft Battery Replacement.\n3.2.1 Make sure replacement batteries are in airworthy condition. Refer to the battery \nmanufacturer maintenance manuals for proper maintenance of lithium batteries. Refer \nto the aircraft maintenance procedures for replacement of lithium batteries.\n3.2.2 The ICA should include the manufacturer’s recommendations for the battery mandatory\nreplacement schedule and periodic maintenance.\n\n3-3\n3.2.3 Installation of lithium batteries differs from aircraft system to aircraft system. Refer to \nthe applicable aircraft manuals to remove and install batteries.\n3.2.4 When replacing batteries, check for corrosion and moisture on the battery interfaces.\n3.2.5 When replacing batteries, check for short circuit to battery case such as insulation \nresistance test.\n3.2.6 The maintenance record should reflect all battery replacements. Record the expiration \ndate of the battery.\n3.2.7 The lithium batteries should be replaced with an approved battery for the specific \naircraft application.\n3.2.8 Deep discharge may result in a potentially unsafe condition. Replace the battery based \non the manufacturer’s recommendation.\n3.3 Aircraft Battery Storage and Handling.\n3.3.1 Storage requirements can vary with the battery type, so follow the manufacturer’s \nrecommended storage procedures to achieve the best results.\n3.3.2 Record the date of charging. If the battery is not used within the manufacturer’s \nrecommended interval, service the battery per the manufacturer’s recommendation.\n3.3.3 To maintain battery integrity, follow the manufacturer’s recommendation for charged \nbatteries being held in “ready for service” areas.\n3.3.4 Handling procedures and precautions vary with battery size and configuration. Follow \nthe manufacturer’s recommendation to prevent mishandling of the battery.\n3.3.5 Follow the manufacturer’s recommendation procedure to prevent electrostatic discharge \nduring storage and handling.\n3.3.6 For packaging and shipping, follow the manufacturer’s recommended procedures. \n3.3.7 Check batteries before use for any leakage or deformity. Do not use the batteries if there \nis any evidence of leakage or deformity.\n3.3.8 Aircraft vibration and/or contact oxidation can result in poor electrical connections. \nEnsure proper connector maintenance procedures are followed.\n3.3.9 Observe the following precautions when handling lithium batteries:\n3.3.9.1 Do not store lithium batteries with other hazardous or \ncombustible materials.\n3.3.9.2 Do not heat or incinerate lithium batteries.\n\n3-4\n3.3.9.3 Do not dispose of lithium batteries with other waste unless allowed by \napplicable regulations.\n3.3.9.4 Use special care in handling lithium batteries. TYPICAL SPECIAL CONDITION (SC) AND INTENT FOR EACH SC \nFOR PARTS 23, 25, 27, AND 29\nSpecial Condition Requirement #1: \nSafe cell temperatures and pressures must be maintained during any foreseeable charging or \ndischarging condition and during any failure of the charging or battery monitoring system not \nshown to be extremely remote. The rechargeable lithium battery installation must preclude \nexplosion in the event of those failures. \nThe intent of this SC requirement: \nThe cells within the lithium battery system shall be designed to minimize the impact of \nself-sustained, uncontrolled increases in cell temperature or pressure, as a result of any \nforeseeable charging or discharging condition. Clean as required.\n3.1.8.2 Inspect the battery for improper installation (loose terminal screws, battery \nterminal links, or connector).\n3.1.8.3 Inspect the battery mounting.\n3.1.8.4 Inspect for evidence of physical damage including heat \ndamage/discoloration.\n3.1.9 Batteries in a rotating stock must be functionally checked at the manufacturer’s \nrecommended inspection intervals. Some failure modes may include degraded charge \nretention capability, settling of particulates, or other damage due to prolonged storage.\nBatteries in rotating stock may also require periodic servicing per the manufacturer’s \ninstructions.\n3.2 Aircraft Battery Replacement.\n3.2.1 Make sure replacement batteries are in airworthy condition. Refer to the battery \nmanufacturer maintenance manuals for proper maintenance of lithium batteries. Refer \nto the aircraft maintenance procedures for replacement of lithium batteries.\n3.2.2 The ICA should include the manufacturer’s recommendations for the battery mandatory\nreplacement schedule and periodic maintenance.\n\n3-3\n3.2.3 Installation of lithium batteries differs from aircraft system to aircraft system. Refer to \nthe applicable aircraft manuals to remove and install batteries.\n3.2.4 When replacing batteries, check for corrosion and moisture on the battery interfaces.\n3.2.5 When replacing batteries, check for short circuit to battery case such as insulation \nresistance test.\n3.2.6 The maintenance record should reflect all battery replacements. Record the expiration \ndate of the battery.\n3.2.7 The lithium batteries should be replaced with an approved battery for the specific \naircraft application.\n3.2.8 Deep discharge may result in a potentially unsafe condition. Replace the battery based \non the manufacturer’s recommendation.\n3.3 Aircraft Battery Storage and Handling.\n3.3.1 Storage requirements can vary with the battery type, so follow the manufacturer’s \nrecommended storage procedures to achieve the best results.\n3.3.2 Record the date of charging. If the battery is not used within the manufacturer’s \nrecommended interval, service the battery per the manufacturer’s recommendation.\n3.3.3 To maintain battery integrity, follow the manufacturer’s recommendation for charged \nbatteries being held in “ready for service” areas.\n3.3.4 Handling procedures and precautions vary with battery size and configuration. Follow \nthe manufacturer’s recommendation to prevent mishandling of the battery.\n3.3.5 Follow the manufacturer’s recommendation procedure to prevent electrostatic discharge \nduring storage and handling.\n3.3.6 For packaging and shipping, follow the manufacturer’s recommended procedures. \n3.3.7 Check batteries before use for any leakage or deformity.
